metadata.title: Darnell Mooney does not catch pass Sunday
metadata.description: Darnell Mooney did not catch either of his two targets in the Giants 34-27 loss against the Saints.
metadata.analysis: Mooney had one carry for 20 yards. He remains off the fantasy radar.

metadata.title: Darnell Mooney - Questionable with neck issue
metadata.description: Mooney (neck) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Saints, Ross Jackson of WWL Louisiana reports.
metadata.analysis: Mooney sustained a neck injury in the second half of Sunday's game. The wide receiver will need to be thoroughly vetted for a significant injury before potentially being allowed to return to the contest. Charlie Jones will operate as the Giants' No. 3 wide receiver while Mooney is absent.

metadata.title: Darnell Mooney Questionable to Return With Neck Injury
metadata.description: New York Giants wide receiver Darnell Mooney (neck) is questionable to return to Sunday's Week 6 matchup against the New Orleans Saints, according to Art Stapleton. Mooney entered the contest having dealt with a neck issue during the practice week, he participated fully Thursday and Friday and carried no injury designation into Sunday. The veteran contributed a 20-yard rushing attempt before the latest injury update, but his availability for the remainder of the afternoon is uncertain. It remains unclear whether he aggravated his previous injury or suffered a separate neck issue. Malik Nabers and tight end Isaiah Likely remain New York's primary receiving options, while Malachi Fields could see additional playing time if Mooney cannot return.

metadata.title: Darnell Mooney (neck) upgraded to full participant Thursday
metadata.description: Darnell Mooney (neck) was upgraded to a full participant at practice on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: The veteran was able to practice in a full capacity on Thursday, despite being limited by a neck issue on Wednesday. He should play in Week 6 but will continue to be irrelevant from a fantasy perspective moving forward.

metadata.title: Darnell Mooney - Full practice Thursday
metadata.description: Mooney (neck) was a full participant in Thursday's practice, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
metadata.analysis: Barring a setback, Mooney will play in Week 6 versus the Saints. However, the 28-year-old hasn't been productive in his five regular-season appearances in 2026, amassing eight receptions (17 targets) for 109 yards.

metadata.title: Darnell Mooney - Limited by neck injury
metadata.description: Mooney (neck) was a limited participant during Wednesday's practice, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
metadata.analysis: Mooney may have tweaked his neck during the Giants' 27-27 tie to the Commanders in Week 5, when caught two of seven targets for 14 yards. He'll have two more opportunities to increase his practice participation and avoid an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Saints. Mooney has just eight catches (on 17 targets) for 109 yards through five games and has taken a back seat in the passing game behind Malik Nabers and tight end Isaiah Likely.

metadata.title: Darnell Mooney (neck) limited in practice Wednesday
metadata.description: Darnell Mooney was limited in practice on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: Mooney remains off the fantasy radar in his current role.

metadata.title: Darnell Mooney quiet in Week 5 tie
metadata.description: Darnell Mooney caught two of his seven targets for 14 yards in the Giants' 27-27 tie with the Washington Commanders in Week 5.
metadata.analysis: Mooney has underwhelmed to begin the season in the New York offense, finishing with less than 50 receiving yards in each of the first five contests. The wideout can be left off rosters in all formats ahead of a Week 6 contest against the New Orleans Saints.

metadata.title: Darnell Mooney catchless in win Sunday
metadata.description: Darnell Mooney failed to haul in either of his two targets in Sunday's 36-24 win over the Arizona Cardinals.
metadata.analysis: The veteran wideout wasn't able to get in on the action on Sunday, despite New York's offense actually finding success against Arizona's defense. He shouldn't be expected to produce much moving forward, especially from a fantasy perspective.

metadata.title: Darnell Mooney's Volume a Concern Against Vulnerable Cardinals Secondary
metadata.description: New York Giants wide receiver Darnell Mooney has caught six of eight targets for 95 yards in three full games this season. With a healthy Malik Nabers and tight end Isaiah Likely, Mooney's target volume hasn't been high. In those three games, Matt Nagy's Giants offense ranks 28th in pass attempts and 30th in pass rate over expected, and with backup quarterback Jameis Winston in the lineup, the team may lean even more on the run. Mooney faces an Arizona Cardinals secondary that has allowed the second-most fantasy points to wide receivers this season. With Cardinals cornerbacks Will Johnson (neck) and Garrett Williams (achilles) ruled out and Max Melton (toe) questionable, Mooney and the Giants' receivers should be able to produce. However, the team's run-heavy system and Mooney's lack of targets should keep him out of fantasy lineups despite the favorable matchup.

metadata.title: Darnell Mooney - Totals 29 yards vs. Tennessee
metadata.description: Mooney caught two passes on three targets for 20 yards and logged a nine-yard carry during the Giants' 12-7 win over the Titans on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Mooney has logged two catches in each of the first three games of the regular season, and his 95 receiving yards are third-most on the Giants behind Isaiah Likely (124) and Malik Nabers (96). The Giants will stay home for Week 4 against the Cardinals, whose defense has given up the second-most fantasy points to wide receivers this season.

metadata.title: Darnell Mooney ineffective in win Sunday
metadata.description: Darnell Mooney caught 2-of-3 targets for 20 yards in Sunday's 12-7 win over the Tennessee Titans.
metadata.analysis: New York's offense failed to score even  a single touchdown on Sunday, so it's no surprise that Mooney individually didn't have a good showing either. He caught just two passes for 20 yards, and fantasy managers shouldn't expect him to return to relevance for however long QB Jameis Winston is starting for the Giants.

metadata.title: Rain Could Limit Darnell Mooney's Volume Against Titans
metadata.description: New York Giants wide receiver Darnell Mooney may struggle to find more volume in Week 3 against the Tennessee Titans. Through two games, Mooney has been efficient, hauling in four of five targets for 75 yards and averaging just 4.8 half-PPR fantasy points per game. With starting quarterback Jaxson Dart (knee) set to miss the remainder of the season, Jameis Winston is set to take over the offense. Under Matt Nagy, the Giants could become even more run-heavy as they look to limit Winston's turnovers. The forecast in East Rutherford calls for heavy rain and wind at kickoff, which should lead to a low-scoring, run-heavy script for both the Titans and the Giants. Despite his strong efficiency to start the season, Mooney should remain out of starting lineups in Week 3.

metadata.title: Darnell Mooney - Leading receiver in loss
metadata.description: Mooney caught two of three targets for 48 yards in Monday night's 28-6 loss to the Rams.
metadata.analysis: Mooney led the team with 48 receiving yards in what was a disappointing outing for New York's offense. Starting quarterback Jaxson Dart suffered a knee injury on the first possession of the game, and he is expected to be sidelined for the foreseeable future. Mooney will look to continue to build chemistry with new starter Jameis Winston in Week 3 against the Titans.

metadata.title: Darnell Mooney leads team in receiving Monday
metadata.description: Darnell Mooney hauled in 2-of-3 targets for 48 yards in Monday night's 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams.
metadata.analysis: The veteran was technically the team's leader in receiving yards on Monday night, but he did it with just 48 over the course of the game, which still left him with a poor fantasy total. He shouldn't be rostered in most league formats for the foreseeable future.

metadata.title: Darnell Mooney Settles Into a Modest Role to Start the Season
metadata.description: New York Giants wide receiver Darnell Mooney found himself occupying a modest role during Week 1 against the Dallas Cowboys. It wasn't a small role by any means, but it also wasn't enough to prompt fantasy managers to scramble and place a waiver claim for him. Mooney played 57% of the snaps in the season opener, catching two passes for 27 yards. He was nestled into the No. 3 spot on the depth chart behind Malik Nabers and Malachi Fields. Given the youth and upside of those two receivers, Mooney is unlikely to pass either of them in the pecking order. In fact, he needs to continue producing at a decent level to fend off any sort of competition from Odell Beckham Jr. Mooney didn't handle enough snaps or targets in Week 1 to suggest that he should be a fantasy starter, but he's still a fine player to target on the waiver wire in deeper leagues with 14+ teams.

metadata.title: Darnell Mooney - Two catches in Week 1
metadata.description: Mooney caught both of his targets for 27 yards in Sunday night's 28-20 victory over Dallas.
metadata.analysis: Mooney was on field for 39 of the team's 69 total offensive snaps, 11 fewer than rookie Malachi Fields. He appears to have settled in as New York's primary slot receiver as the regular season gets underway, and veteran Odell Beckham may be his biggest competition for the role moving forward.

metadata.title: Darnell Mooney quiet in win Sunday
metadata.description: Darnell Mooney caught two passes for 27 yards in Sunday night's 28-20 win over the Dallas Cowboys.
metadata.analysis: The veteran wideout had a quiet game in a win over the Cowboys. He contributed just 27 yards on two catches, which obviously didn't amount to much from a fantasy perspective. He isn't expected to be relevant moving forward, especially with rookie Malachi Fields there to compete for the WR2 spot behind Malik Nabers.

metadata.title: Darnell Mooney Listed as Giants' WR2
metadata.description: The New York Giants' unofficial depth chart has Darnell Mooney as the team's No. 2 wide receiver entering the year behind Malik Nabers (knee), according to ESPN's Jordan Raanan. Rookie Malachi Fields and veteran Odell Beckham Jr. are the backups to Nabers and Mooney after the Giants recently cut Darius Slayton from the 53-man roster. Mooney comes to the Big Apple in 2026 after a down year in his second season with the Atlanta Falcons, in which he caught 32 of 72 targets for 443 yards and only one touchdown in 15 starts. The year before, the 28-year-old former fifth-rounder from Tulane had a resurgent season, catching 64 passes for 992 yards and a career-high five touchdowns in 16 starts. After the season-ending injury to Calvin Austin III (knee) and the release of Slayton, Mooney could be a sneaky deep-league option off the waiver wire to begin the 2026 season. Right now, he is only rostered in 1% of Yahoo leagues. Mooney's best year came in 2021 with the Chicago Bears, when he posted an 81-1,055-4 line in 17 games played in his second year in the NFL.

metadata.title: Darnell Mooney's Path to Targets Keeps Shrinking
metadata.description: New York Giants wide receiver Darnell Mooney is getting squeezed out of the fantasy conversation. He signed in March with a decent path to targets after a 32-catch, 443-yard season in Atlanta, but rookie Malachi Fields has spent the summer making that path a lot less comfortable. Fields caught all three of his targets for 34 yards and a touchdown in the preseason opener, then kept building momentum in camp. SNY reported this weekend that the third-round pick could work in tandem with Malik Nabers, even though the Giants' unofficial depth chart still lists Mooney ahead of him. That's the problem for Mooney. New York also kept Darius Slayton and Odell Beckham Jr., while Nabers is working toward a Week 1 return. RotoBaller now has Fields at WR76 in half-PPR formats and Mooney down at WR106. Mooney still has speed and familiarity with offensive coordinator Matt Nagy, but there just isn't much room left for a dependable target share.

metadata.title: Darnell Mooney - Could have path to No. 3 role sans Austin
metadata.description: Mooney could have a chance to open the season as the Giants' No. 3 receiver after Calvin Austin (knee) sustained a torn ACL in Tuesday's practice, Jordan Ranaan of ESPN.com reports.
metadata.analysis: Before injuring his right knee, Austin looked primed to play a significant role as the Giants' slot receiver, but the team is now expected to take a committee approach to that position in the wake of his season-ending injury, per Dan Duggan of The Athletic. Along with Mooney, fellow wideouts Malik Nabers (knee) and Odell Beckham and tight end Isaiah Likely could also get more chances to work in the slot. Ranaan notes that Mooney -- who produced a 32-443-1 receiving line on 72 targets in 15 games with the Falcons in 2025 -- turned in one of his best practices of the summer Tuesday, which could prompt the coaching staff to carve out more snaps for him with the first-team offense.

metadata.title: Giants Have Fielded Calls on Darnell Mooney
metadata.description: The New York Giants have reportedly fielded calls about trading wide receiver Darnell Mooney, according to Art Stapleton. Mooney signed a one-year, $3 million contract with the Giants this offseason, with expectations that he would pair with star wideout Malik Nabers on the outside. While Mooney has had a strong training camp, rookie receiver Malachi Fields' emergence could prompt the team to trade Mooney for value and let Fields operate with the starters this season. The former Falcons' receiver struggled in 2025, hauling in 44% of his targets for 443 yards and one touchdown in 15 games. Fantasy managers should keep a close eye on this Giants' receiver situation, as any move involving Mooney and veteran Darius Slayton could open the door for Fields to have a bigger role this season.

metadata.title: Darnell Mooney Leads Giants' Wideouts in Targets During Training Camp
metadata.description: New York Giants wide receiver Darnell Mooney has been the most targeted wide receiver at training camp. According to Giant Insider, Mooney has consistently worked with the first-team offense and is expected to play a major role in 2026. The former Bears and Falcons wide receiver is coming off a disappointing year, totaling just 443 yards and one touchdown in 15 games last season. Mooney signed a one-year, $3 million deal with the Giants and is competing for a prominent role alongside star Malik Nabers. With Nabers missing most of training camp while recovering from a torn ACL, Mooney has made an impact. From a fantasy perspective, Mooney is a long shot to be a major factor, as the team is expected to be run-heavy and use a lot of heavy personnel.
